observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon DSLR camera body with a lens mount area visible; the top has a Nikon logo and the model marking appears to be D7000.
Photo 1 shows the camera from a different angle with the lens cap removed/lying nearby; the lens mount and front controls are visible.
Both photos show the camera inside/against damaged cardboard packaging; no clear view of screen, buttons, ports, or any included accessories besides what’s implied by the seller.
No photo shows the camera powered on, no viewfinder/screen image, and no shutter/recording proof.

claims.claim: The camera is working perfectly fine.
claims.evidence: No photo/video shows the camera powered on, taking a photo, or displaying any error-free screen/EVF output.

claims.claim: I am selling with 2 batteries and a silicone case.
claims.evidence: Photos show the camera body and a lens cap; there is no clear photo of two batteries or a silicone case.

risks.risk: Camera may not be fully functional (shutter, autofocus, sensor, buttons, or power issues). Photos cannot confirm operation.
risks.proof: A short video of powering on + navigating menus + taking a photo (showing the captured image on screen) and then powering off.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as needing testing/possible faults).

risks.risk: Battery count/accessories may be missing or not the correct type/capacity.
risks.proof: Photo/clip showing both batteries side-by-side with labels/part numbers and the silicone case in the same frame.
risks.if_unproven: Price as camera only (no guaranteed extra batteries/case).

risks.risk: Lens mount/contacts or body may be damaged (cosmetic damage is visible on packaging; body condition not fully shown).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the lens mount contacts, tripod mount, ports (USB/AV), and any cracks/scratches on the body edges.
risks.if_unproven: Price at a lower condition tier until body condition is confirmed.

risks.risk: Model could be misread (D7000 marking not fully verifiable from the provided angles).
risks.proof: Photo of the model/serial label on the bottom plate and a clear shot of the top model text.
risks.if_unproven: Price conservatively for the identified model only if confirmed; otherwise treat as unknown Nikon DSLR for pricing.

proof_requests: Power-on proof: video showing menu + taking a test photo + playback on screen/EVF.
Show both batteries clearly (labels/part numbers) and the silicone case in photos.
Close-ups: lens mount contacts, bottom serial/model label, and all ports/buttons.
response.reason: The photos identify a Nikon D7000 body, but the key seller claims (working perfectly fine; includes 2 batteries and a silicone case) are not verifiable from the images. Without power-on/test and accessory proof, pricing would be guesswork.
